# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 4 (Bu-Vb Pc4)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc4
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 4
**Title (English, from literature):** Instructing a lay person to memorize the Teaching

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 4, entitled *Padasodhamma* ("Instructing a lay person to memorize the Teaching"), is an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule is formulated as: *Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannaṁ padaso dhammaṁ vāceyya, pācittiyaṁ* ("Whoever monk teaches the Dhamma line by line to an unordained person commits a pācittiya") [Dutt 1957]. Monastic regulation broadly treats this as an offense to recite sacred texts or teach the word of the Buddha line by line to those who are not fully ordained, although the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*) interprets the rule specifically as targeted against an improper pedagogical method of instructing a novice (*śrāmaṇera*) [Dutt 1957; Clarke 2009].

 DharmaNexus confirms these cross-language relationships through automatic alignment with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse of standard Vinaya analysis and casuistry clauses between this rule and other Vibhaṅga sections (especially Pācittiyas 5, 23, 74, 75, 76, and 77), the *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18), and the subcommentarial *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule and its full vibhaṅga has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
